senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; שָׁלַח , v. Ges. Thes. ed. Rödiger s. v.) plate, table.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 68b:2">Ab. Zar. 68ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>עולה על ש׳ של מלכים</he> is brought up on the royal table (is considered a delicacy).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 4:1:5">Y. Kidd. IV, beg. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>גירי שׁוּלְחַן מלכים</he> proselytes who joined for the sake of the royal table (to be members of the royal household); <cite ref="Yevamot 24b:3">Yeb. 24ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="U00437"><he>שׁוּם</he> II</cite>.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:3">Ab. III, 3</cite> <he>שלשה שאכלו על ש׳ אחד … משֻׁלְחָנוֹ של מקום</he> when three persons eat at the same table, and hold conversation about the Law, they are considered as if eating from the table of the Lord (the altar), opp. <he>זבחי מתים</he>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 55a:1">Ber. 55ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Chagigah 27a:2">Ḥag. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>שלחנו של אדם וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="K01046"><he>כָּפַר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Beitzah 20b:8">Bets. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>שלא יהא שׁוּלְחָנְךָ מלא וכ׳</he> lest thy own table be full, and thy Master’s table (the altar) be empty.

Kidd. III, 2 ואם הראה על הש׳ וכ׳ but if (he is a banker and) shows her the stipulated amount on the table (the money not being his own), she is not betrothed; a. fr.—Esp. the table for the show-bread in the Temple.
<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 11:5">Men. XI, 5</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>שׁוּלְחָנוֹת</he>, <cite ref="U00420"><he>שֻׁלְ׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 6:4">Shek. VI, 4</cite> <he>שלשה עשר ש׳ וכ׳</he> there were thirteen tables in the Temple.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 1:3">Ib. I, 3</cite> <he>בחמשה עשר בו ש׳ היו יושבין וכ׳</he> on the fifteenth of Adar changing tables were put up in the city, on the twenty-fifth, in the Temple; a. fr.
